title: The gate follows the reviewer's current row after a fallback

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: S49 relay later note. Stickiness is per role (decision 115), so after the reviewer falls back to its second row the gate, which uses the reviewer's lineup (docs/design.md:580) and resumes its session, starts again on the first row with only its own records (currentEntry, internal/engine/engine.go:156). Owner 2026-10-23: the gate follows the reviewer's current row.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/engine.go:156-185` (currentEntry): for the gate, start from the reviewer's current index when the gate has no record of its own, and advance on the gate's own failures from there.
- `internal/engine/fallback_test.go`: tests.
- `docs/design.md:392-396` and `:580`: say the gate follows the reviewer's row.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestGateStartsOnTheReviewersCurrentRow: the reviewer fell back to row 2; the gate's first round uses row 2.
- TestGateFallsBackFromTheReviewersRow: a rate-limited gate round on row 2 moves to row 3, and never back to row 1.
- TestGateWithItsOwnLineupIsUnchanged: a gate with its own lineup entries keeps the old behaviour.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: 1. Write the failing tests first. 2. In currentEntry, when role is the gate and rec.Lineup[gate] is empty, seed cur from currentEntry(rec, reviewer). 3. Keep records walking as now. 4. Update docs/design.md.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- go test -race -count=1 ./internal/engine
- go test -race -count=1 ./...
- go vet ./...
- gofmt -l .
- slicer check
- adj lint
